title: NightWatch Common Definitions
description: Shared definitions for all NightWatch contracts. Semantics source: NightWatch Architecture v1.4 §5.5 (ID rules, time semantics), §22.5.4 (runtime time semantics).

ulid.description: ULID: 26 chars, Crockford Base32 (excludes I, L, O, U), lexicographically sortable (monotonic). Source: WorkRequest §5.5.

iso8601_utc.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp, always Z-suffixed. All wall-clock timestamps use this. Source: §5.5 / §22.5.4.

duration_ms.description: Duration in milliseconds (monotonic-clock measured). Source: §5.5 duration rule.

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency key. Duplicate keys with differing payloads must yield an idempotency-conflict error (CTL_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT / ISS_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT / AUD_REPLAY_MISMATCH). Source: §22.5.4.

checksum.description: SHA-256 checksum, optionally sha256:-prefixed, lowercase hex.

credential_reference_name.description: Credential variable REFERENCE NAME only (e.g. ORDER_API_TOKEN). Never a value. Source: §13.1.

id_session.description: Session object ID. Source: §5.5 prefix table.

id_run.description: Run object ID. Source: §5.5 prefix table.

id_exec.description: Execution request ID. Source: §5.5 prefix table.

id_plan.description: Test plan ID. Source: §5.5 prefix table.

id_case.description: Test case ID. Source: §5.5 prefix table.

id_draft.description: Issue draft ID. Source: §5.5 prefix table.

id_issue.description: Publish receipt ID (issue-domain internal object). Source: §5.5 prefix table.

id_audit.description: Audit event ID. Source: §5.5 prefix table.

id_lease.description: Injection lease ID. Source: §5.5 prefix table.

session_state.description: Session state machine states. Source: §7.2. 'blocked' is a recoverable state entered from running.

cleanup_status.description: Cleanup outcome; cleanup timeout is preserved as an independent result. Source: §22.5.4 / §14.

run_outcome.description: Run terminal outcome. Source: §5.7 (exit code / timeout / cancel).

reproducibility.description: Reproduction history: attempts, failures, rate = failures/attempts in [0,1]. Source: §14.1 item 9 / §16.
